narrative_purpose: Grounds Pandora's human clock problem in measured Earth experience by showing the managed protocol required to keep rover teams on a day only thirty-nine minutes longer than ours.
subject: A Mars rover operations specialist sits at an unbranded console in a dark control room, face tired and posture slumped while a wall of windows shows ordinary terrestrial daylight outside. Beside the workstation stands a broad clinical blue-enriched light panel bathing the face and eyes; on a small tray near a closed sleeping berth lies one plain melatonin tablet and a glass of water. In the background, three colleagues occupy successive work bays at visibly different states of alertness and local daylight, suggesting a schedule that shifts later each day without any readable clocks.
scene: A quiet terrestrial mission-control annex adapted for Mars time, isolated from normal office lighting but unable to hide the changing Earth day outside.
camera: Medium-wide observational view across the main operator, light panel, window and sleep berth in one coherent room.
light: The therapeutic panel supplies controlled cyan-blue key light; normal daylight at the window is muted and displaced; small amber task light marks the treatment tray.
palette: Deep indigo control room, cyan therapy light, teal screens with no glyphs, pale daylight, sparse amber at the treatment tray.
style: Painterly human-factors field observation, clinically believable and unglamorous, not futuristic command-centre spectacle.
detail_level: Clear exhausted posture, blue light panel, outside daylight mismatch and treatment tray; consoles remain soft and unreadable.
composition: Operator and blue panel occupy the left centre; daylight window opens on the right; berth and treatment tray anchor the lower right; background staff recede in a shallow diagonal. Leave dark air beside the face and window for callouts.
consistency_notes: This is a control team on Earth following Mars time, not astronauts on Mars. The blue light and melatonin are deliberate treatment tools; the window shows Earth's changing daylight.
negative_prompt: no text, no logos, no readable clocks, no sci-fi HUD, no astronauts, no Mars surface outside, no medical drama, no photo or CGI look
